chunks: And it is narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said:
O Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ, buying flour is humiliation, buying wheat is honor, and buying bread is poverty. So seek refuge in Allah from poverty.

key_terms.الدَّقِيقِ: flour, mentioned here as a symbol of diminished self-sufficiency
key_terms.الْحِنْطَةِ: wheat, presented here as a sign of honor
key_terms.الْخُبْزِ: bread, mentioned here in relation to poverty
key_terms.شِرَاءُ: the act of purchasing or buying

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach about buying flour, wheat, and bread?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a moral teaching about dignity, self-sufficiency, and avoiding conditions associated with dependence and poverty. It concludes by urging believers to seek refuge in Allah from poverty.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3971 - It is narrated from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani that Abu Abdullah (as), said:
"O Abu Al-Sabbah! Buying flour is humiliation, buying wheat is honor, and buying bread is poverty. So seek refuge with Allah (swt) from poverty."
